{"baseRefName":"main","body":"Closes #392

## Summary

A detailed, reproducible performance report of Nona v0.18.0 against Node.js 22, Deno 2.9 and Bun 1.4, built the way engines and AOT compilers are compared publicly, with numbers for every claim.

- **`PERFORMANCE.md`**: a new dated top section (version, commit, machine, runtime versions; the v0.13.0 section is marked superseded and kept) with a summary table of the geometric mean of the Nona/Node ratio per category, then per-benchmark tables with median and interquartile range of ≥ 10 runs (5 for the long real programs and Benchmarks Game), peak RSS, executable size, build time, an HTTP table, Node's JIT warm-up curve against Nona's flat profile, instruction counts and routine profiles, an analysis of wins and losses with their causes, and a "Method" section surveying JetStream 2, Are-We-Fast-Yet, the Benchmarks Game, "VM Warmup Blows Hot and Cold", Bun/Deno/Node comparisons and the Static Hermes/Porffor/Hopc write-ups, with links.
- **Workloads**: the existing micro-benchmarks and `bench/real` (acorn, marked), plus lodash 4.17.21, Prettier 3.6.2, the `log-scan` string/RegExp case of #387–#389, a 20 MB JSON file, ten program-corpus programs, the 14 **Are-We-Fast-Yet** JavaScript benchmarks unchanged (fetched at a pinned commit by `bench/awfy/fetch.mjs`, with the suite's licenses), nine **Benchmarks Game** programs written for the repository after the problem descriptions (`bench/game/`; the game's own sources are on salsa.debian.org, unreachable from the VM, and its fastest JS entries use worker threads), and `bench/http`.
- **Correctness gate**: every case compares its result between runtimes (`check` values, the AWFY harness's `verifyResult`, md5 of stdout for whole programs). All 14 AWFY benchmarks, all 9 game programs and all real programs compile and produce the same output on Nona; no mismatch was found. Deno cannot import lodash's CommonJS file (no default export); the report lists it as a failure rather than dropping the row.
- **Scripts**: `bench/report.mjs` (suites `startup,corpus,micro,real,awfy,game,profile`) regenerates every table and writes raw runs to `bench/results/` (git-ignored); `bench/lib/{stats,measure,metrics}.mjs` hold the statistics, process measurement and metric labels; `tests/bench-report.test.ts` (in the `frontend` suite) tests them and checks that every micro-benchmark metric has a label and category.
- README, README.ru, the site's translated performance pages and `bench/README.md` updated with the new figures; CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.

## Headline numbers (Linux x64, shared 2-vCPU VM, Node.js 22.22.0)

| Category | Cases | Geomean Nona / Node |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start-up and memory | 12 | **×0.1** (hello world 1.3 ms / 1.05 MB / 1.07 MB executable vs 38 ms / 45 MB) |
| Compute | 16 | ×2.1 |
| Allocation, objects, collections | 10 | ×2.4 |
| Strings, RegExp, JSON | 20 | ×4.5 |
| I/O and event loop | 5 | ×2.8 |
| Real programs | 9 | ×11 |
| Are-We-Fast-Yet (steady state) | 14 | ×13 |
| Benchmarks Game (whole process) | 9 | ×11 |

Largest losses: anything on the RegExp VM (×64–×355: log-scan `match`, regex-redux, marked, lodash `camelCase`), inline-cache misses on class instances (n-body ×33–×37, Richards ×18, Havlak ×28; `rt.shapeLookup` + `rt.compareStrings` dominate the profiles), call overhead (×6–×8), GC/heap growth (binary-trees ×7.7, RSS 1.5–3× Node's on allocation-heavy programs), promises (×10), `writeFileSync` (×7.6). HTTP throughput is at Node's level with a quarter of the memory. Follow-up issue proposals (nine) are in the PR thread's companion file.

## Testing

Linux x64: `npm run build` (typecheck), `npm run format:check`, `node --test dist/tests/bench-report.test.js dist/tests/suites.test.js dist/tests/source-budget.test.js dist/tests/ci-changes.test.js dist/tests/architecture-doc.test.js` (all pass). Benchmarks run with `node bench/report.mjs` suite by suite (about 40 minutes in total), `bench/http/run.sh` twice.

## Known limitations

- Linux x64 only; Windows x64, arm64 and macOS numbers were not taken (no runner here) and are listed as a follow-up.
- The VM is shared: ratios within ×1.5 are marked as noise; IQRs are printed everywhere.
- Nona executables cannot run under valgrind (frame probes below RSP), so the instruction counts use QEMU for Nona and callgrind for Node.js, at small scales where Node is still in its interpreter; the report says so and uses them only for Nona's routine breakdown.
- `12_fs` still writes to `/tmp` (Windows run needs a temp path); `bench/report.mjs --suite profile` needs `qemu-x86_64`, `objdump` and `valgrind`.
- `deno compile` and Node SEA sizes were not re-measured (v0.7.0 table kept).
